plan.planning_summary: This study tests three distinct strategy axes for dual-bandpass mid-IR filter design on CaF2 substrate. Route 1 explores periodic quarter-wave stacks with high index contrast (Si/SiO2) to achieve broad transmission with natural stopbands. Route 2 tests Fabry-Perot cavity resonance for precise dual-band control with defect layers in mirror stacks. Route 3 examines mixed-material periodic designs (Si3N4/MgF2) for reduced stress and alternative index matching. These axes are genuinely independent: periodic stacks rely on Bragg reflection physics, cavity designs rely on resonant transmission, and mixed materials test whether lower index contrast with more layers can match high-contrast fewer-layer performance. All routes respect the 24-layer maximum, no-metal constraint, and substrate requirement from the original request. The CaF2 substrate ambiguity is resolved by using the specific dataset name Daimon-20.

routes.title: High-Contrast Periodic Quarter-Wave Stack for Dual-Bandpass
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A periodic Si/SiO2 quarter-wave stack with 10 layer pairs can achieve simultaneous high transmittance at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm while maintaining stopbands at 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm through natural Bragg reflection harmonics.
routes.design_principle: High index contrast (Δn ~ 2.4 for Si/SiO2 in mid-IR) creates wide stopbands with fewer layers. Quarter-wave optical thickness at the geometric mean of passbands produces transmission windows at harmonic positions that can align with the two gas absorption bands.

design_variables: individual thicknesses of all 20 coating layers
manufacturing_considerations: Si and SiO2 are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
20 layers within 24-layer maximum
no metal layers used
Daimon-20 substrate requires low-temperature deposition compatibility
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for periodic multilayers
Bragg reflection condition for stopband formation
High index contrast reduces required layer count per L01
expected_advantages: Fewer layers needed due to high Δn
Natural harmonic transmission windows may align with dual passbands
known_risks: Quarter-wave design may not precisely align both passbands simultaneously
Stopband edges may not match required 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm exactly
Si absorption in mid-IR may reduce peak transmittance

Stack structure: Air | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | CaF2 (Daimon-20). Materials: si, SiO2 (Kischkat). Substrate: CaF2 (Daimon-20). Maximum 24 layers respected.

routes.title: Dual-Cavity Fabry-Perot Filter for Precise Band Control
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A dual-cavity Fabry-Perot structure with two defect layers embedded in Bragg mirrors can independently tune transmission peaks at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm while maintaining deep stopbands between and outside the passbands.
routes.design_principle: Fabry-Perot cavities produce narrow transmission peaks at resonant wavelengths determined by cavity optical thickness. Two cavities with different thicknesses create two passbands. Bragg mirror stacks on both sides provide stopband rejection. This approach follows L09's 4-cavity F-P design adapted for dual-band transmission.

routes.title: Mixed-Material Periodic Stack with Reduced Index Contrast
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A Si3N4/MgF2 periodic stack with 12 layer pairs can achieve comparable dual-bandpass performance to high-contrast Si/SiO2 designs while offering reduced mechanical stress and better thermal matching to Daimon-20 substrate.
routes.design_principle: Lower index contrast (Si3N4/MgF2 Δn ~ 1.0 vs Si/SiO2 Δn ~ 2.4) requires more layers for equivalent stopband depth but may provide better mechanical stability and thermal compatibility. This tests whether layer count can compensate for reduced contrast within the 24-layer limit.

routes.title: Dual-cavity bandpass filter using ZnS/MgF2 on Daimon-20 substrate
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 22-layer stack with two half-wave cavities separated by Bragg mirror sections will produce two transmission peaks centered near 4.25 μm and 4.65 μm, with stopbands at 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm showing suppressed transmittance relative to the passbands.
routes.design_principle: Bandpass filters work by creating resonant cavities bounded by high-reflectance Bragg mirrors. Quarter-wave stacks create high reflectance outside the design wavelength; inserting half-wave spacer layers creates transmission peaks. Two cavities with different optical thicknesses produce two passbands. The index contrast between ZnS (high) and MgF2 (low) provides sufficient reflectance per interface.
routes.proposed_topology: air | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | Daimon-20
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 22 dielectric layers
cavity spacer layer positions and thicknesses within the fixed 22-layer topology
soft_objectives: keep total layer count at exactly 22 layers
manufacturing_considerations: all layers must be depositable by conventional physical or chemical vapor deposition
no metal layers included
total layer count is 22, within the 24-layer maximum
ZnS and MgF2 are both standard IR coating materials
theory_basis: Quarter-wave Bragg mirrors produce high reflectance when optical thickness equals λ/4 at the design wavelength
Half-wave spacer layers in a Bragg stack create transmission resonances (Fabry-Perot cavities)
Higher index contrast between alternating materials increases stopband width and reflectance per pair
Multiple cavities produce multiple transmission peaks; cavity optical thickness determines peak position
Normal incidence simplifies design as polarization splitting is not a concern
expected_advantages: ZnS/MgF2 pair provides good index contrast in mid-IR from recalled knowledge
22 layers leaves margin within the 24-layer constraint for potential refinement
Dual-cavity topology directly addresses the two-passband requirement
All materials are conventional IR dielectrics without metals
known_risks: Refractive index values for ZnS and MgF2 at 4-5 μm are recalled approximately; actual dispersion may differ and would need to be confirmed from the material registry
Daimon-20 substrate index at these wavelengths is recalled but not verified; the registry data will determine actual performance
The exact layer count of 22 was chosen from memory of similar filters; optimal count may be different
Stopband rejection level is uncertain without running the solver; may require more layers or different cavity spacing
Thermal stability and adhesion of ZnS/MgF2 on Daimon-20 is not addressed in this optical-only design
The two passbands are close together (4.25 μm and 4.65 μm center); achieving both with adequate separation from stopbands may be challenging
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 22-layer dielectric multilayer filter on a CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate for normal incidence from air. Use alternating ZnS and MgF2 layers. The stack sequence is: air | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate. Optimize all 22 layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in the 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm bands while minimizing transmittance in the 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm bands. No metal layers. Total layer count is fixed at 22 dielectric layers.

research_influence: L01 motivated Route 1's high index contrast Si/SiO2 approach with justification that Δn ~ 2.4 reduces layer count for mid-IR filters
L09 motivated Route 2's dual-cavity Fabry-Perot design based on their 4-cavity F-P filter for mid-IR dual-channel applications
L05 supported Route 3's material selection by reviewing conventional IR dielectric multilayer structures and fabrication techniques
L26 provided validation for all-dielectric Si/SiO2 and Si3N4 approaches in IR filtering applications
L28 confirmed the 4.2 μm and 4.7 μm wavelength targets align with CO2 and CO detection requirements
unresolved_decisions: Daimon-20 substrate refractive index dataset selected from the four CaF2 options to resolve ambiguity
Exact trade-off between passband width and stopband depth not predetermined - will emerge from optimization
Whether 24-layer maximum is sufficient for Si3N4/MgF2 design remains to be tested in Route 3
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all three routes fail to achieve best_target_score above 0.7 with positive tightest_margin after full iteration, the problem requires either relaxed layer count constraint, alternative material system outside conventional dielectrics, or acceptance of single-band rather than dual-band design

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
